notes:
Summary: Thundernova builds orchestration for mid-to-large contact centers; evaluating Redwood for agent-assist + automated summarization and to harden behavior under incident bursts/seasonal spikes. Current pain: production outages during sale events and marketing pushes — queue stacks up, agent-assist timeouts, downstream tools rate-limit. Key metrics they care about: concurrent live guidance sessions (target support 6k baseline, bursts to 22k), peak OLTP requests to LLM endpoints (target <200ms p50 for short agent prompts, <800ms p90 for summary batches), and token cost per ticket. They want predictable tail latency under 3x baseline load.

POC scope requested: dedicated GPU pool with autoscale thresholds, synthetic spike harness that can reproduce 10–25k concurrent sessions, end-to-end observability (token-level cost + latency breakdown), forced fallback policy to smaller quantized model on overload, and prefix/kv caching for repeated customer context. Also want runbook for graceful degradation: route to cached responses, degrade to extractive summarization, open tickets to on-prem summarizer if external endpoints constrained.

Security/compliance: must pass SOC2 checklist, require SAML SSO and audit logging shipped to their Splunk instance, optional HSM/KMS integration for keys, EU data residency for EU customers (they operate EU contact centers). Legal wants 30–90 day retention controls and ability to purge PII on request.

Conversations/quotes: "We can tolerate slightly higher p50 but p99 spikes kill agent workflows" — Head of Ops. "If you can show consistent fallbacks and a deterministic cost model during spikes, procurement moves fast" — Dir. Product.
